title: Eight Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）　|　核心词汇：expectation　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 expectation 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my mother ① held an expectation that no teacher in the school would have named, and she said the holding was the whole of the winter. The ② expectation, meaning the hope itself and not the promise, ran eight winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an expectation, she said, is the only thing in a school that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ expectation in that school had the same short note beside it, and the ④ expectation at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the child and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An expectation, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my mother said the naming is the part that fills eight winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the expectation was the whole of the term, meaning the standard and not the hope. The ⑥ expectation, meaning the standard and not any of that, is the only thing in a term that everybody waits for and nobody names; expectation, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both a hope and a standard. He said the standard is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ expectation had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ expectation of the whole thing, my mother wrote in January, was one school and eight winters of naming; expectation, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ expectation I remember is the one named in the report, which closed in 1969 and is still described as the quietest in the school. An ⑩ expectation, my grandmother said in 1971, is the only one that improves by being named; every expectation, she said, is a standard that has agreed to look like a hope. She said the standard was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 期望；期待（指学校里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 期望（指那一份本身，与承诺相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold an expectation 怀有一份期望
D. n. 期望（指留给孩子的那一份）
E. n. 期望（抽象总称，指一所学校的期待之事）
F. n. 期望（指报告上写到、被说出的那一份）
G. n. 要求；标准（指一个学期里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）
H. n. 标准（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西）

items.q: held an expectation that no teacher in the school would have named
The expectation, meaning the hope itself and not the promise
the expectation at the far side

answers.why: hold an expectation 意为“怀有一份期望”，1959 年母亲怀有一份学校里没有一位老师肯说出的期望。
expectation 意为“期望”，指那一份本身而不是承诺，它经过了八个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
expectation 意为“期望”，指学校里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一张短短的字条。
expectation 意为“期望”，指留给孩子的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
expectation 意为“要求、标准”，指一个学期里人人都等却无人说出的那样东西，叔叔说这份要求就是那个学期的全部。
expectation 意为“标准”，指人人都等却无人说出的那样东西而不是那一份期望，是学期里人人都等、却无人说出的东西。
expectation 意为“期望”，指报告上写到、被说出的那一份，到 1966 年这一份成了报告里的一行。
expectation 意为“期望”，母亲一月写道，整件事的期待之事是一所学校和八个冬天的说出。
expectation 意为“期望”，我记得的是报告上说出的那一份，1969 年结束了，至今仍被说成学校里最安静的一份。
expectation 为抽象总称，祖母 1971 年说，一份期望是唯一会因为被好好说出而变得更好的东西。
